name: Federal Reserve

summary.text: The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States. In 2008 the Federal Reserve Bank of New York created the Maiden Lane vehicles to take on assets tied to the Bear Stearns rescue and the AIG bailout, and retained BlackRock to manage them. AIG's credit default swap counterparties, including Goldman Sachs, were effectively paid in full (at par), which drew criticism at a 2010 Congressional Oversight Panel hearing. In 2014, ProPublica and This American Life published secret recordings by former New York Fed examiner Carmen Segarra that they said illustrated a culture of deference to banks at the New York Fed.

facts.claim: In 2008 the New York Fed created Maiden Lane LLC, Maiden Lane II and Maiden Lane III, lending about $28.8 billion, $19.5 billion and $24.3 billion. They bought Bear Stearns mortgage assets, AIG's mortgage-backed securities, and CDOs underlying credit default swaps AIG had written.

facts.claim: The New York Fed retained BlackRock to manage the Maiden Lane assets. House Oversight Chairman Henry Waxman questioned awarding the role 'without competition'; the Fed cited extreme time constraints.

facts.claim: In 2014 ProPublica and This American Life reported on about 46 hours of meetings secretly recorded by former New York Fed examiner Carmen Segarra. In one recorded meeting the week before she was fired, her boss repeatedly tried to persuade her to change her conclusion that Goldman Sachs lacked a conflicts-of-interest policy.

facts.claim: GAO's July 21, 2011 audit (GAO-11-696), directed by the Dodd-Frank Act and covering Federal Reserve Board emergency actions from December 1, 2007 through July 21, 2010, found that the Reserve Banks, mainly the New York Fed, awarded 103 contracts worth $659.4 million from 2008 through 2010 to support emergency work, that a few contracts accounted for most vendor spending, and that the Reserve Banks relied more extensively on vendors for programs that assisted a single institution than for broad-based programs. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act directed GAO to conduct a one-time audit of the emergency loan programs and other assistance authorized by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System / The Reserve Banks relied more extensively on vendors for programs that assisted a single institution than for broad-based programs

facts.claim: GAO-11-696 found that the New York Fed took steps to manage conflicts of interest for its employees, directors and program vendors, but that opportunities exist to strengthen its conflict policies, and that its code did not specifically prohibit investments in certain nonbank institutions that received emergency assistance. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: the New York Fed took steps to manage conflicts of interest for its employees, directors, and program vendors, but opportunities exist to strengthen its conflict policies / Its code did not specifically prohibit investments in certain nonbank institutions that received emergency assistance

facts.claim: GAO-11-696 recommended that the Federal Reserve revise its acquisition policies to ensure competition and favorable terms for acquired services. GAO noted that in a few cases the Federal Reserve Board authorized a Reserve Bank to lend to a limited liability corporation to finance the purchase of assets from a single institution, the structure used for the Maiden Lane vehicles. (GAO finding.)
facts.quote: the Fed should revise their acquisition policies to ensure competition and favorable terms for acquired services / in a few cases, the Federal Reserve Board authorized a Reserve Bank to lend to a limited liability corporation (LLC) to finance the purchase of assets from a single institution

connections.claim: The New York Fed retained BlackRock Financial Management to manage the Maiden Lane portfolios in 2008. On March 24, 2020 it retained BlackRock Financial Markets Advisory as investment manager for its Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility.

connections.claim: The Federal Reserve has supervised Goldman Sachs since approving its application to become a bank holding company in September 2008. ProPublica's 2014 reporting on Carmen Segarra's recordings described New York Fed supervisors pressing her to soften a finding that Goldman lacked a conflicts-of-interest policy.

connections.claim: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System is a member central bank of the Bank for International Settlements. The Board and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York are both members of the BIS-hosted Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, which sets international bank capital and liquidity standards.

connections.claim: The Federal Reserve Board authorized, and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York created and lent to, Maiden Lane LLC (authorized March 16, 2008; $28.8 billion lent at the June 26, 2008 closing), Maiden Lane II LLC ($19.5 billion) and Maiden Lane III LLC ($24,339 million principal at closing, with a $5.0 billion AIG equity contribution).

openQuestions: The GAO-11-696 passages retrieved in this session do not name BlackRock or state which Maiden Lane contracts were awarded noncompetitively; the report's figure on contracts and fees by procurement method and its vendor conflict-of-interest section should be read directly before any claim about BlackRock's award method is attributed to GAO.
The recommendation sentence ('revise their acquisition policies to ensure competition and favorable terms') was returned truncated by the search; confirm the wording in the Highlights page.
